assertions.given: The owner opens the capture form.

assertions.when: The owner submits with a blank URL or an address that is not an absolute http or https URL.

assertions.given: The library already contains a record for a URL, including a version differing only by surrounding whitespace, host casing, or a trailing slash.

assertions.when: The owner tries to save that address again.

assertions.given: At least one owner-created collection exists and the owner is saving a new link.
assertions.negative: The record must not remain in the inbox after a successful save and must not be filed in both collections at once.

assertions.when: The owner selects that collection in the capture form and submits a valid URL.

assertions.negative: Saving must not require or create an account, must not transmit the library contents to a server, and must not make the record visible to any other person.
assertions.then: The record is written only to that profile's local storage, the library remains reachable without signing in, and no shareable or public address for the record is produced.
assertions.when: The owner saves a link that already exists nowhere in the library.

assertions.given: The owner's library contains a known number of records.
assertions.negative: The product must not convert browsing activity, page visits, or application use into any record without an explicit owner save.
assertions.then: The record count and contents stay exactly as they were, and nothing appears in the inbox.
assertions.when: The owner opens the library, browses pages elsewhere, or leaves the application idle without invoking save.

assertions.then: The updated values are shown and persisted, the record keeps its identifier and original creation time, and collection counts reflect any move.
assertions.when: The owner edits the title, description, tags, URL, or collection and saves.

assertions.given: The library already has an inbox and may have other collections.
assertions.negative: A blank name or a case-variant duplicate must not create a second collection or silently replace the existing one.
assertions.then: A new empty collection with a stable identifier appears in the sidebar and collection pickers and persists after reopening.
assertions.when: The owner creates a collection with a nonblank name that does not collide after trimming and case folding.

assertions.given: A record is in the inbox and an owner-created collection exists.

assertions.then: The record leaves the inbox view, appears under the target collection, both counts change, and the assignment survives closing and reopening the application.
assertions.when: The owner moves the record from the inbox to that collection.

assertions.given: A record is displayed with a collection assignment.

assertions.when: The owner attempts to move it to a collection that no longer exists in storage.

assertions.given: A saved record exists with a valid URL.

assertions.then: The original page opens in a new browser tab, the library remains in its current view, and the record's last-opened time and optional open count are updated.

assertions.given: A record exists whose external page cannot be opened or whose URL has become invalid.

assertions.when: The owner selects one collection in the organization sidebar.

assertions.when: The owner enters a word that appears only in a URL, hostname, description, or tag, with any casing.

basis.statement: The product exists so a person can retain an external page seen but not processable now, and later find it again and return to the original page.

A bookmark manager is defined by four properties: records anchored to an external address, deliberate capture rather than automatic logging, a persistent accumulating personal library, and owner-controlled organization and retrieval. The form of organization is an implementation choice.
The first actor step is an explicit save of a page the user wants to remember, made while browsing and without requiring immediate processing.
At save time the user may choose one simple category such as 待购, 家居改造, or 以后看看, and the user can create categories and move existing records between them.
An unsorted link may first enter a default category and be moved to a better place later.
When ready to act, the user opens the personal library and locates the earlier link by browsing categories or by keyword search, both scoped to records they already saved.
The final actor step is opening a record and returning to the original page to continue buying, reading, or referencing; the application does not take over content consumption.

At the pinned commit the README describes the application as privacy-focused and local-first, storing bookmarks in browser IndexedDB with no accounts, servers, or tracking, and the declared store is a Dexie database named BookmarkDB with one bookmarks table. This is static document and code evidence only, not a runtime claim.

The upstream Bookmark type contains id, title, url, hostname, favicon, description, tags string array, isPinned, isArchived, visitCount, createdAt, and visitedAt; it has no collection or folder field, no separate tag entity, no deletion marker, and no manual ordering field.

Upstream organization is tag-only: sidebar tag counts are aggregated from each record's tags array and sorted alphabetically, tags are filtered as multi-select AND with a reset action, and no collection creation, naming, or move interface appears in the observed files.

The upstream search field matches only the record title as a lowercased substring, with a placeholder explicitly saying search by title; URL, hostname, description, and tags are not searched. The library is split into Home and Archived tabs.

Upstream save validation requires a valid http or https URL, a title of at most 100 characters, a required description of at most 280 characters, and one to five tags of at most 30 characters each; the URL input additionally hard-caps entry at 100 characters while the validation schema sets no URL length limit.

Upstream metadata retrieval is a manually triggered button that calls api.microlink.io for title, description, and logo, then proxies the logo through images.weserv.nl and a Google favicon endpoint; failures are only logged to the console and the form remains manually fillable.

The upstream Visit action calls window.open with the record URL in a new tab using noopener and noreferrer, and also serves Copy URL from the same overflow menu; the card title is not itself a link, so opening requires the menu.
The same Visit action sets visitedAt to the current time and increments visitCount before writing the record back to IndexedDB; no other observed action changes those values.

Upstream sorting places pinned records first, then applies the chosen strategy: recently visited by visitedAt descending, most visited by visitCount descending, with createdAt descending as the fallback and newest-added as the default.

Upstream offers Home and Archived tabs, toggles isArchived while clearing the pin on archive, and exposes deletion only for archived records: the record is removed from IndexedDB immediately and a toast Undo re-inserts it. There is no trash view, and unarchived records cannot be deleted from the observed interface.

Upstream record identifiers are random values created at save time and the primary key is that identifier rather than the URL; the observed save path performs no same-URL lookup, so duplicate addresses can coexist and no merge logic appears in the observed files.

Design proposal: organize the product with one optional level of owner-created collections plus a mandatory default inbox, because the scenario speaks of 归类, moving between 归类, and a 默认归类, while the upstream tag-only model cannot express an unsorted waiting area. Tags stay optional labels rather than a second navigation structure.

Design proposal: require only the URL to save; derive the title from fetched metadata or the hostname, and leave description, tags, and explicit collection optional, because the scenario is about capture before processing. This deliberately relaxes the upstream requirement for a description and at least one tag.

Design proposal: persist the single-owner library in local browser storage and state explicitly that it is scoped to one browser profile. No account system is introduced, and cross-device synchronization is excluded rather than implied by the word persistent.

Design proposal: make opening the original page a directly visible primary action on the record and its detail view rather than a hidden menu item, keep the library open behind the new tab, and let opening update optional usage metadata without changing the record's filing state.

Design proposal: search titles, URLs, hostnames, descriptions, and tags together, combine the query with one active collection, and default to newest-added ordering with optional recently-opened and most-opened orderings. This broadens the upstream title-only search because users often remember a domain or a phrase from the description.

Design proposal: prevent a second record for the same normalized URL and route the owner to the existing record, using trimming, host lowercasing, and trailing-slash removal as the baseline. The upstream model uses a random primary key and contains no duplicate check.

Design proposal: treat metadata fetch as an optional, explicitly invoked convenience that discloses any third-party request and never blocks manual entry or saving. The upstream use of microlink and weserv is reference only, not a required dependency.

Design proposal: do not carry the upstream field length ceilings or the 100-character URL input cap into the product definition, because they are implementation details unsupported by the scenario; the new product's limits remain open pending product confirmation.

Design proposal: keep tags as optional free-form string labels on records, usable for recall and search, without a tag sidebar, tag counts, or tag administration, because the scenario's organizing axis is a single collection and upstream tag-only navigation would compete with it.

Design proposal: leave pinning, archiving, unread flags, and read-later state out of the core, because archive is easily mistaken for another collection and the scenario defines a single organizing axis with no clutter-management step.

Design proposal: keep deletion out of the core flow; if removal is later added it must be recoverable and clearly distinct from collection organization, rather than copying the upstream coupling of archive with immediate physical delete and toast undo.

gaps.resolution: Impose no reference-level ceilings; validate only the URL scheme and shape, and set practical limits later from usability evidence.
gaps.statement: No evidence justifies limits on URL, title, description, or tag length, or a maximum tag count for the new product. Upstream's 100-character URL input cap conflicts with its own validation schema and was not behaviorally tested.

gaps.resolution: Treat usage metadata as optional supporting information; acceptance of the core depends on opening the page, not on statistics.
gaps.statement: Whether retaining open counts and last-opened times is acceptable is not confirmed. Upstream records both and sorts by them, while the scenario only asks to return to the page.

gaps.resolution: Keep the library add form as the only capture surface for this boundary; revisit only if capture away from the application becomes a stated requirement.
gaps.statement: The scenario describes saving while browsing but does not name a capture channel. Browser extension, bookmarklet, and mobile share target are excluded from this web-only boundary, so today a save starts from the library's add action with a URL at hand.

gaps.resolution: Keep tags as searchable free-form fields on records; exclude a tag sidebar and tag administration from the core boundary.
gaps.statement: Tags are preserved as optional labels following the scenario's evidence and upstream behavior, but whether tag filter checkboxes, tag counts, or tag management belong in the product is not confirmed.

journeys.completion: A deliberately saved link survives the session, is visible in the personal library, and can be reopened at its original address without the product recreating or hosting the page.
journeys.goal: Keep a page met during browsing with almost no interruption, then come back to the live page when the owner actually needs it.
journeys.name: Save now, return later
journeys.recovery: If metadata or icon retrieval fails, the owner saves with only the URL and a derived title. If opening fails, the URL stays visible for copying or correction. If storage fails, the form stays populated and the save can be retried.

steps.success: The add action opens the capture form with the URL field ready and the inbox preselected.
With only a URL entered, the record is saved into the inbox with a hostname-derived title and appears in the library immediately.
The saved record is still listed in a later session, and opening it launches the original page in a new tab while the library stays open.

journeys.completion: The library's organization is entirely owner-defined, records can be refiled indefinitely, and collection assignments are durable rather than session state.
journeys.goal: Turn an unsorted accumulation into a personally meaningful structure by creating a collection and moving saved records into it, with the result surviving restart.
journeys.name: Triage the inbox into collections
journeys.recovery: If a collection name is blank or collides, creation is refused with an explanation and the inbox stays intact. If a move target is missing, the record stays where it was and the owner can retry from a refreshed sidebar.

steps.success: The owner opens the inbox and sees the records saved without an explicit collection.
A new named collection such as 待购 or 家居改造 is created empty and appears in the sidebar.
The chosen record moves from the inbox to the new collection and both counts update.
The owner adds a clarifying title or description without changing the record's identity or collection.
After reopening the application, the collection still contains the moved record and the inbox no longer lists it.

journeys.completion: The owner finds a record they already chose to keep and reaches the live resource; the product behaves as a retrieval tool for known references, not as a search engine for unseen pages.
journeys.goal: Locate a previously saved page from a remembered word, domain, or rough filing location and return to it.
journeys.name: Find a link remembered only vaguely
journeys.recovery: A no-results state preserves the query and active collection and offers to clear or broaden it. If the URL is broken, the record stays in the library with its stored address available for correction.

steps.success: A remembered word from the title, domain, description, or tag narrows the library to candidate records.
If several candidates remain, browsing the likely collection reduces the list to the relevant records.
The owner identifies the intended record and opens the original page, while the library keeps the record for future retrieval.

product_shape.audience: An individual web user who meets pages faster than they can act — product pages, tutorials, documentation, inspiration, things to buy or revisit — keeps them on purpose, and comes back weeks or months later to use them.
product_shape.boundary: One owner deliberately saves external web page addresses. Each record stores the URL plus minimal owner-editable metadata, persists across sessions in that browser profile's local storage, and sits in exactly one owner-created collection or in the default inbox. The owner browses collections, searches their own records, reorders the current result set, edits or moves a record, and opens a record to the live page in a new tab. The library keeps the reference and its metadata only; page content stays on the web and is never consumed, rendered, or archived inside the product.
product_shape.delivery_profile: Single-owner, local-first web application with one personal library per browser profile. No account, server, collaboration, or sharing in the modeled boundary. Upstream repository evidence is a static reading of a pinned commit that was never installed, built, or run; no runtime behavior of that implementation is claimed.
excluded: Accounts, sign-in, identity verification, and any multi-tenant access control
Collaboration, invited members, shared collections, and permissions beyond the single owner
Public profiles, public collection pages, social discovery, and follower networks
Cross-device or cross-browser synchronization; persistence is explicitly limited to one local browser profile
Browser extension, bookmarklet, mobile share target, bulk import from browsers or other services, and export
Preserved page copies, reader view, offline archives, and read-later queues
Automatic capture of browsing history or any record created without an explicit owner save
Pinning, archiving, unread flags, reminders, and manual ordering as core capabilities
Bulk edit, bulk move, multi-select, and selection-wide operations
Broken-link detection, link repair, and duplicate merge tooling beyond the save-time duplicate response
Deletion, trash, and restore flows in the core; removal semantics remain an open product question
Full-text search over page content, and search over anything other than the owner's own saved records
Tags as independently managed entities, tag hierarchies, tag counts, or tag rename and merge administration
product_shape.name: Bookmark Manager — Personal Link Library
product_shape.value: A durable, private, growing library of references: every saved link points at its live web page, can be filed into a simple owner-defined collection or left in an inbox, and can be found again by browsing or searching, so the owner returns to the original page instead of searching the web for it a second time.

roles.data_scope: All records, collections, tags, and metadata in this browser profile's library. No other person's data exists inside the product boundary, and no role can read or modify another profile's library.
roles.goal: Save links with almost no friction, keep them organized in a way that makes personal sense, and find and reopen them later.
roles.name: Library owner

rules.statement: Records enter the library only through an explicit owner save action; browsing activity is never converted into records automatically, and no background process may append to the library on its own.
Every record is anchored to an absolute http or https URL; the record is a reference to content owned by the external site, not a copy of that content.

Saved records, their metadata, and their collection assignments persist across sessions in the owner's local browser storage; they are not confined to a single page session, and persistence is explicitly limited to that one browser profile.
The library always contains one default inbox; a save without a collection choice lands there, and the owner can later move the record into any collection or back to the inbox.
A record is filed in exactly one collection at a time; organization is a single-level, owner-controlled structure, while tags remain optional free-form labels rather than a second hierarchy.

The library keeps one record per normalized URL: comparison trims surrounding whitespace, lowercases the host, and removes a trailing slash; a matching save is reported together with the existing record instead of creating a second entry.

Retrieval operates only on the owner's own saved records: search matches title, URL, hostname, description, and tags as case-insensitive substrings, and collection browsing narrows that same set; results never include pages the owner has not saved.
The default order is newest-added first; optional recently-opened and most-opened orderings apply only to the current result set and fall back to newest-added for ties so no record disappears.

Only the URL is required to save; the title may be fetched or derived from the hostname, and description, tags, and an explicit collection choice are optional so capture costs seconds. Length ceilings for URL, title, description, and tags are not fixed by the available evidence.

Opening a record launches its URL in a new browser tab with noopener and noreferrer semantics and leaves the library view in place; a successful open updates last-opened time and open count, while a failed open updates neither.

The library is private to one owner in one local browser profile, with no accounts, collaborators, public pages, or tracking; any third-party metadata request is an explicit, disclosed, optional action rather than a silent side effect of saving.

The product does not fetch, render, or persist the referenced page's body as a library object; there is no reader view, preserved snapshot, or read-later queue in the boundary, so the library guarantees the reference rather than the content.

Collection names are trimmed, nonblank, and unique after case folding; the default inbox is fixed and cannot be renamed or recreated as an owner collection, so every collection is an unambiguous navigation target.

Organization stays revisable: a record can be moved or edited at any time, and renaming a collection preserves its records and identifier; the product never imposes a structure the owner did not choose.

scope_options.name: Core personal library
scope_options.rationale: The irreducible product: deterministic save from a URL, durable local records, an inbox plus owner-created collections, single-record move and edit, collection browsing and cross-field search, and return to the original page. Every element traces to the fixed scenario or the leaf's defining core; nothing here comes from upstream feature breadth. Shipping this slice alone yields a usable private library.

scope_options.name: Optional metadata assistance
scope_options.rationale: Fetched titles and descriptions reduce typing but must never be a save precondition, because the scenario requires keeping a link before deciding to process it. This slice adds only the explicitly invoked fetch, must disclose any third-party request, and must leave manual entry fully usable when the service fails.

scope_options.name: Collection renaming
scope_options.rationale: A lightweight structural-maintenance capability separated from the core because the scenario requires creating and moving, not renaming. When added it must preserve record membership and identifiers and must never allow the fixed inbox to be renamed.

scope_options.name: Usage-based ordering
scope_options.rationale: Newest-added ordering suffices for a young collection; recently-opened and most-opened orderings help a large accumulated library. They stay optional because the scenario asks to find a link rather than to control sorting, and retained open statistics carry unresolved privacy questions.

surfaces.name: Personal library
surfaces.purpose: Show the owner's records in the active collection, let the owner search, reorder, open, move, or start a save, and make an accumulating library feel navigable.

query.bulk: Not provided: selection, bulk move, and bulk edit are outside the core boundary.
query.export: Not provided and no export format is defined; interoperability is outside this product boundary.
query.filter: Exactly one collection at a time, including the default inbox; upstream-style tag checkboxes and multi-tag AND filtering are outside this boundary.
query.pagination: No pagination requirement is established; record volume is unknown and the core renders the loaded result set in one scrollable list.
query.search: Case-insensitive substring match over title, URL, hostname, description, and tags of the owner's own records; an empty query applies no text filter.
query.sort: Newest-added descending by default, with optional recently-opened and most-opened orderings, each falling back to newest-added for ties.

Per-record actions for open, edit, and move

states.empty: No records exist: the view explains that saved links will accumulate here and offers the add action and the empty inbox; it never fabricates sample bookmarks.
states.error: Local storage cannot be read or written: a banner states that the library is unavailable or unsaved and offers retry; it never presents stale data as current.
states.forbidden: Not applicable: the product has exactly one owner role and no shared or public view, so no other role can be denied access here.
states.loading: A first-load state explains that the local library is being read and shows a placeholder list without inventing records.
states.no_results: The active query or collection scope yields no records: the view names the query and collection and offers to clear the search or switch collection.

query.bulk: Not applicable: exactly one record can be saved or edited per submission.
query.export: Not applicable: the form neither imports nor exports data.
query.filter: Not applicable: there is no result set to filter; the collection selector is an input choice, not a filter.
query.pagination: Not applicable: the form edits one record at a time.
query.search: Not applicable: the capture form is not a search surface and has no result query.
query.sort: Not applicable: form fields are presented in a fixed task order.

states.empty: A new save form starts blank except for the default inbox selection and a URL placeholder; there are no prefilled sample records or invented collections.
states.error: Validation messages appear inline next to the affected fields; a storage failure appears as a form-level error with all values retained.
states.forbidden: Not applicable: only the owner can reach the capture surface, so no permission-denied state exists.
states.loading: While metadata is being fetched the form stays open with a progress indicator and the owner's entered values preserved; manual entry remains possible.
states.no_results: Not applicable: this is a form rather than a result list, so absent metadata is shown as an empty optional field instead of a search-result emptiness.

surfaces.name: Organization sidebar
surfaces.purpose: Act as the library's structural map: expose the inbox and every owner-created collection with counts, support browsing into one, and allow creating or renaming collections.

query.bulk: Not applicable: collection operations act on one collection at a time.
query.export: Not applicable: the sidebar has no export action.
query.filter: Not applicable: it exposes all collections; narrowing happens in the library list.
query.pagination: Not applicable at this boundary's scale; the collection count is small and no paging is defined.
query.search: Not applicable: the sidebar is a short structural list, not a searchable result set.
query.sort: Collections follow a stable sidebar order; free-text queries never re-rank them.

sections: Default inbox entry with record count
Owner-created collection list with record counts
Create-collection control and name validation
Rename control for non-default collections

states.empty: Only the default inbox exists; the sidebar explains that the owner may create the first collection and offers the create control.
states.error: Collections cannot be read: the sidebar shows an error with retry and the library falls back to the inbox only.
states.forbidden: Not applicable: there is no non-owner role and no sharing, so no collection is hidden for permission reasons.
states.loading: The sidebar shows a compact placeholder until collections are read from local storage.
states.no_results: Not applicable: an empty collection is a valid destination and is shown with a zero count rather than treated as a failed result.

surfaces.name: Record detail
surfaces.purpose: Show one record's identity and metadata, with returning to the live page as the primary action and the ability to edit or move the record.

query.bulk: Not applicable: actions apply to the selected record only.
query.export: Not applicable: no export action exists on the record detail.
query.filter: Not applicable: there is no result set to filter, only a collection assignment to change.
query.pagination: Not applicable: one record is shown at a time.
query.search: Not applicable: the detail view shows one record; search belongs to the library surface.
query.sort: Not applicable: a single record has no ordering.

states.empty: Not applicable: the detail surface opens only for an existing record, so there is no empty-record variant.
states.error: If the record is no longer present in local storage, the panel closes with a notice and the library refreshes.
states.forbidden: Not applicable: only the single owner can open a record, and no record is shared or restricted.
states.loading: Not applicable in the core because the record is already in the loaded list; if a refresh is required, a short loading label is shown rather than a blank panel.
states.no_results: Not applicable: the surface presents one selected record and has no result set.
